# Usage Evidence

This page gives the facts about the prices, the models, and the usage that claudetto uses.
It also gives the measurements of one heavy week of an earlier release (0.x) and what they mean.
Read it to learn what drives the usage, and which values are measured.
The source of each number is named in its row or line.
Source labels are official, binary, measured, reported, and inference.

## Summary

- One Max 20x week reached 100% of the weekly limit at $1,854 (measured, see [the measured week](#the-measured-week)).
- Three things drive the usage: the context per turn, the subagent fan-out, and the `general-purpose` agent.
  The model choice is not one of them.
- Turns set the cost, not tool calls.

## Prices

The API list prices are per million tokens.
They were checked on 2026-10-13 (official).
Source: `https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing`.

| Model | Base input | 5-minute cache write | Cache read | Output |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Fable 5.1 | $10 | $12.50 | $0.25 | $50 |
| Opus 5.5 | $4 | $5 | $0.20 | $20 |
| Sonnet 5.5 | $2 | $2.50 | $0.10 | $10 |
| Haiku 5.5 (prompts up to 100,000 tokens) | $0.10 | $0.125 | $0.01 | $0.50 |
| Haiku 5.5 (prompts over 100,000 tokens) | $0.50 | $0.625 | $0.05 | $2.50 |

- The Haiku 5.5 price rises above 100,000 prompt tokens.
  A long task on Haiku 5.5 can reach the higher price.
  The long-prompt price is derived from the table, and claudetto has no rule that moves a task to another model.
- The Sonnet 5.5 cache read is $0.10 per million tokens.
  An older text of this wiki gave $0.20, and that value is stale.
- Anthropic publishes no subscription multiplier.

## Fable Limit

Fable draws from the regular weekly limit.
It is not an extra pool.
These facts are from the Anthropic help pages, as the old text of this page cited them.
They are not checked again in this run.

- On Max and on Team or Enterprise premium seats, Fable can use up to 50% of the weekly limit.
- On Pro and on standard Team or Enterprise seats, Fable runs on usage credits.
- The binary labels the `seven_day_overage_included` limit as the Fable limit (binary).

A Fable weekly figure of 0% does not give free headroom.
Each model has at most the remaining share of the weekly limit.

## Cache Facts

- An effort change keeps the prompt cache.
  A model change rebuilds the prompt cache, because the cache is kept for each model.
  This is official, from the prompt caching page.
- The cache of the main conversation lives 1 hour on a subscription within its limits.
  It lives 5 minutes on usage credits or an API key.
  Subagents use 5 minutes (official, as the old text of this page cited it, not checked again in this run).
- A prompt after the TTL, and a `/compact` after it, write the whole context again.
- From Claude Code `2.1.287`, the `SessionStart` input for `resume` and `fork` has `prompt_cache_likely_expired` (binary, not checked again in this run).

## Effort

- Claude Code defaults Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 to `medium` (official, not checked again).
- No hook event fires on an effort change (binary).
- A model switch loses the prompt cache (official).
  So a plugin that switches the model at plan mode, as `opusplan` does, pays a cache write at each switch.

## Model Aliases

- The `haiku` alias resolves to Haiku 5.5 on the Anthropic API.
  It resolves to Haiku 4.5 on Bedrock, Vertex, and Foundry (documents only, no probe there).
- A full model ID such as `claude-haiku-5-5` works in the `agent.spawn` hook.
- `maxEffortLevel: max` causes no clamp.
  An effort of `max` that a hook sets arrives as `xhigh`.
  The cause is probably an account limit for each model (unverified).

## The Measured Week

One Max 20x week (2026-09-21 to 09-28) reached 100% of the weekly limit.
The figures come from a scan of the local transcripts (measured).
The repository does not hold that scan.
The transcripts start on 09-25, so the figures are a lower bound.

The week ran under the config of an earlier release (0.x), not under 1.0.0 or claudetto.
Most of the week ran before 0.5.0 moved `implementer` to Sonnet 5, so the `implementer` row ran mostly on Opus 5.5.
The source is the 0.26 text of this page, in git commit `af3071f4` (`wiki/Usage-Evidence.md`, line 22).
The figures show the usage pattern of that config.
`implementer` was a custom agent of that release.

| Measure | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Total | $1,854 (Opus 5.5 98.7%) |
| Cost parts | cache reads 64.7%, cache writes 28.1%, output 7.2% |
| Main conversation | 44.9%, context p50 369k, p90 807k tokens |
| `implementer` | 30.7%, 155 runs, median 68 calls |
| `general-purpose` | 17.6%, 87 runs, median 51 calls |
| Calls with context over 150k | 74.7% of cost |
| Subagent cache writes (5-minute TTL) | 71M tokens, about $355 |
| First cache write of a fresh subagent | p50 13.9k, p90 24.8k tokens |
| Main turns that background agents started | 501 of 861, about $385 |

Three things drive the usage.

1. **Context per turn.**
   Each turn reads the whole context again.
2. **Subagent fan-out.**
   Each fresh subagent writes about 14k tokens to the cache before its first tool call.
   Its 5-minute cache expires while it waits on long builds.
3. **`general-purpose` in place of a purpose-made agent.**
   The settings snippet denies `Agent(general-purpose)` ([Settings Snippet](Settings-Snippet)).
   The denial is a setting.
   It is not a proof that the habit stopped.

## The Delegation Share

The `usage` report of claudetto 0.1.0 scanned the local transcripts.
It reported the sessions by entrypoint, the skill calls, the delegation share, and the latest subagent runs.
The report is not in 0.2.0.
The [Sessions](Sessions) add-on replays and audits a session.

- measured, 2026-10-03, 7 days: 976 subagent runs in 25,578 main turns, which is 3.8 per 100 turns.
- measured, 2026-10-03: tool-result tokens per main session, median 19,169, p90 167,675 (253 sessions).

## Turns, Not Tool Calls

Each model turn reads the context again.
So the number of turns sets the cost.

- Independent tool calls in one response take one turn.
  The same calls in sequence take one turn each.
- Claude Code has no general tool that runs several tools in one call (binary).

## Guard Denies of Read-Only Commands

The guard must deny only a command that discards work.
A deny of a read-only command is a false positive, and this section gives their count.

1. A script read each `.jsonl` transcript under `~/.claude/projects/` of each project except claudetto, read-only.
2. It matched each `tool_result` of a `Bash` call that holds the deny text of the guard (`claudetto forbids this destructive action` or `claudetto forbids this command in a subagent`) to the command of its `tool_use`.
3. Each command that changes no file of the project became a must-pass case in the guard lab, with the project folder replaced by `/p`.

- measured, 2026-10-17: 11 guard denies in 511 transcripts of 6 projects.
- measured, 2026-10-17: 10 of the 11 denies were read-only commands: prints, searches, and check scripts that got destructive commands only as string data.
  All 10 came from an earlier checkout of the claudetto source, where the work tested the guard itself.
  The guard of this release allows each of them (measured), so earlier builds of the guard gave these denies (inference).
- measured, 2026-10-17: the other deny, a `git rm -qf` in an unrelated project, discards work, so the deny was right.
- measured, 2026-10-17: the unrelated projects had 0 false denies.
  This sample is small, and most of its denies come from the work on the guard, so it does not show the false-positive rate of normal use.
- measured, 2026-10-17: the read-only command of `design-handoff.md`, with `$(( ))`, was denied in this project, and the shell scan of this release reads `$(( ))` as arithmetic, so it passes.

## The Code Graph Add-On Against `codegraph install`

This is the measure of task 6.9 of the OpenSpec change `claudetto-0-1-0`.
It ran on 2026-10-18 with no model call, from the code and the text of the add-on before and after the change.
`codegraph` was not on the `PATH` of the machine, so this measure did not run `codegraph install`.
The facts about the install come from the vendor source that the change cites (`dist/installer/instructions-template.d.ts`, measured earlier).

| Part of `claudetto-codegraph` | What `codegraph install` alone gives | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SessionStart` hook and its line (46 words, once for each session) | The block in `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` and the MCP instructions name the same commands | Removed. It adds nothing. |
| `SessionStart` sync, sync after an edit, sync after `git` (hook, mod handler, lock) | `codegraph` syncs its own index (the user, 2026-10-18) | Removed with the three controls. About 450 lines of code and tests, and 3 hook entries. |
| `--mcp` option of the check, and `MCP_ADD_COMMAND` | `codegraph install` writes the MCP server | Removed. |
| Skill `codegraph` (466 words, loaded on use) | The MCP tools cover the same questions, but the subagents get only the block | Kept. It is the way to use the CLI with no MCP server, and its text now says so. |
| `claudetto-codegraph-check` | `codegraph status` shows the index, but a missing CLI is a shell error | Kept. It tells a missing CLI from a failed CLI. Not measured against the live CLI. |

The code of the add-on went from 658 lines (the pin of `tools/limits.ts` in 0.1.0) to 201 lines.
The add-on has no hook now, so it adds no process to a session.

## Model Calls of a Hook

In all 4 runs of task 1.10 of the OpenSpec change `claudetto-0-1-0`, the `result` message did not count the model call of an `agent` hook in `total_cost_usd` (measured).
The source is `external/cc-diff-299-300/live/live-checks.md`, check 6.
A hook that calls `$.model.complete` reads the `usage` of that result, so the cost of its call is the cost from that `usage` at the list prices above.
Two calls of a hook to a small model, on 2026-10-16 with Claude Code `2.1.301`, used 798 input and 68 output tokens at $0.0023, and 826 and 11 tokens at $0.0018 (list prices of Sonnet 5.5).
Each call read no cache, so it paid the full input price.

## Community Claims

- True: `/compact` reads the whole conversation to write its summary.
  On a large context it is an expensive request (official).
  `/clear` costs nothing.
- True: `MEMORY.md` loads at every start, up to its first 200 lines or 25 KB (official).
  Topic files in the memory folder do not load at start.
- True: a short `CLAUDE.md` saves usage.
  It loads at every start, and in every subagent that does not set `omitClaudeMd`.
- True: subagents keep large reads out of the main context.
- False: old `.jsonl` transcripts in `~/.claude/projects/` do not go into the context.
  Only `/resume` loads one.
  The settings snippet does not set `cleanupPeriodDays`.
  See [settings snippet keys](Settings-Snippet-Keys).

## Tools That claudetto Does Not Use

| Tool | Reason |
| --- | --- |
| RTK | A JetBrains measurement of 7.6% more cost (reported). |
| Graphify | It fails on large repositories (reported). |
| grepai | It needs embeddings from Ollama or OpenAI, and it has no measurement. |
